concepts.learning_objective: Classify halogen compounds by the number of halogen atoms and the hybridisation of the carbon bearing the halogen.
Name haloalkanes and haloarenes by the IUPAC system and identify them as primary, secondary or tertiary.
Distinguish geminal and vicinal dihalides and relate their common and IUPAC names.

topics.title: Nature of the C-X bond and methods of preparation

concepts.learning_objective: Relate the polarity, length and enthalpy of the carbon-halogen bond to the size of the halogen.
Describe the preparation of haloalkanes from alcohols, hydrocarbons and by halogen exchange.
Describe the preparation of haloarenes by electrophilic substitution and from diazonium salts.
Explain the trends in boiling points of haloalkanes with halogen size and branching.
Explain the low water solubility and the density trends of haloalkanes.
Relate the high melting point of para-dihalobenzenes to molecular symmetry.
Predict the products of haloalkanes with ambident nucleophiles such as cyanide and nitrite.
Describe the SN2 mechanism, its kinetics and the effect of steric hindrance on its rate.
Describe the SN1 mechanism and relate its rate to carbocation stability.
Identify chiral molecules and state how enantiomers differ in their properties.
Predict retention, inversion or racemisation at an asymmetric carbon in substitution reactions.

topics.title: Elimination reactions and reactions with metals

concepts.learning_objective: Predict the major alkene in dehydrohalogenation using Zaitsev's rule.
Decide whether substitution or elimination is favoured from the halide and the base.
Describe the formation of Grignard reagents and the Wurtz reaction of alkyl halides.
Explain the low reactivity of haloarenes towards nucleophilic substitution and the effect of nitro groups.
Explain why halogens are deactivating yet ortho, para-directing in electrophilic substitution.
Identify the Wurtz-Fittig and Fittig reactions of aryl halides with sodium.
State the uses and hazards of dichloromethane, chloroform, iodoform and carbon tetrachloride.
Describe freons and explain how they affect the ozone layer.
Explain why DDT persists and accumulates in living organisms.
